passage:
In the changing room at school in Chennai, Karthik noticed how tall the boys from 9B already were, how deep their voices sounded, while his own stayed high. He compared his chin with theirs, his shoulders too.
Sabina, from the flat next door, met him at the lift holding her cricket bat. "You look like you swallowed a lemon."
"Everyone's growing except me."
"My cousin was shorter than me until last year, and now he's taller than his dad," she said. "Everybody's on a different clock."
Karthik gave a half laugh. That night he read the chapter on adolescence in his science book, ate a proper dinner and went to bed on time. "Not a race," he told the ceiling.

qa.q: What was Sabina holding when she met Karthik at the lift?
qa.a: She was holding her cricket bat.

qa.q: What was Karthik feeling as he compared himself with the boys from 9B?
qa.a: He felt behind and self-conscious, comparing his chin, shoulders and voice, and told Sabina everyone was growing except him.

qa.q: What did Karthik do that shows patience and care for himself?
qa.a: He read about adolescence in his science book, ate a proper dinner, went to bed on time and reminded himself it is not a race. 😊

qa.q: How does Sabina see Karthik's worry?
qa.a: Sabina sees it as a common worry and reassures him with her cousin's example that bodies grow on different clocks, without mocking.

grounding: Shows a teen comparing his puberty with others' and learning that bodies develop at different speeds.

passage: Class teacher's notes, Aparna Menon, 9C, Friday. Madhav has been sitting out of football for two weeks. Today I found out why. While the boys lined up for the team photo, he hung back, and I overheard him ask Joel whether he'd 'ever get a real voice'. Most of the class have shot up this year; Madhav is still one of the smallest, and his voice hasn't dropped. Later, in the empty classroom, I asked how he was. Eyes on his shoes, he said he felt like a little kid next to everyone. I told him bodies grow on their own timetables, some early, some late, and none of it is a race. I also mentioned I'd been the last in my class to grow, which made him smile. I've asked the PE teacher to put him back in goal on Monday and given him a puberty booklet from the school nurse.

qa.q: What did Madhav ask Joel before the team photo?
qa.a: He asked whether he'd ever get a real voice.

qa.q: What was Madhav feeling next to his classmates?
qa.a: He felt small and embarrassed, like a little kid next to everyone who had shot up.

qa.q: How did the teacher support Madhav?
qa.a: By explaining bodies grow on their own timetables, sharing a personal memory, and getting him back in goal with a booklet from the nurse.

qa.q: What would change if Madhav had grown early instead?
qa.a: He might feel just as awkward for standing out in a different way, which shows no timetable is the 'right' one.

grounding: A teacher's note on a teen comparing his later puberty with classmates and being reassured that bodies develop at different speeds.

passage:
Thursday. Dear diary, swimming class was awful again. I'm the only one in our group whose body has properly changed already, and I spent the whole hour with a towel wrapped round me. Sunaina is still tiny, and she kept saying she wished she looked like me, which is funny because I wish I looked like her. At home I stood in front of the mirror comparing myself to the girls in our group, one by one. Then Mummy knocked. I told her, and she laughed gently, not at me. 'Beti, at your age I was the last one. Your Masi was the first. We both hated it.' She said bodies don't read the same calendar and nobody wins a prize for being early or late. I felt a bit better. Tomorrow I'm leaving the towel on the bench, at least for the first lap.
- Sharmila

qa.q: What did Sharmila keep wrapped around her during swimming class?
qa.a: A towel, for the whole hour.

qa.q: Why did Sharmila feel so uncomfortable at the pool?
qa.a: She felt self-conscious and alone, being the only one in her group whose body had already changed.

qa.q: What small step could help Sharmila feel easier at the pool?
qa.a: Leaving the towel on the bench for the first lap, a patient start rather than forcing herself to feel fine at once 🙂

qa.q: How does Sunaina seem to see Sharmila's body?
qa.a: Sunaina wishes she looked like Sharmila, showing the two are comparing in opposite directions.

grounding: A diary showing a teen comparing her early puberty with others and learning from her mother that bodies develop at different speeds.
